exam_guide_revision: Not a certification. Practical Python 3.10-3.14 fluency track; official Python documentation and selected AnyIO/HTTPX docs reviewed 2026-09-19.

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; progressively harder typed code recall provides the scored signal.

authoring_notes: Python Fluency is practical coding retrieval, not beginner trivia or a certification. Questions use progressive recall depth: guided -> recall -> construct -> fluency. Short literals stay on one line where readable, unfamiliar data shapes and intent are explained, and most questions have one meaningful blank.

modules.title: Use Python 3.10 matching and typing syntax

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ 3.10 structural pattern matching can destructure mappings, sequences, and class instances while binding selected values.

reveal.text: Python 3.10 structural pattern matching can destructure mappings, sequences, and class instances while binding selected values.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ {'type': 'user', 'id': int(user_id)}: ... both checks the event shape and captures an integer id.

reveal.text: case {'type': 'user', 'id': int(user_id)}: ... both checks the event shape and captures an integer id.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ capture name by itself matches almost anything; use literal/class/subpattern structure when validation is intended.

reveal.text: A capture name by itself matches almost anything; use literal/class/subpattern structure when validation is intended.

source_refs.title: What's new in Python 3.10 — pattern matching

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ 3.10 allows union types to be written with |, such as str | None, instead of typing.Optional or typing.Union.

reveal.text: Python 3.10 allows union types to be written with |, such as str | None, instead of typing.Optional or typing.Union.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ parse(value: str | bytes) -> str: ... uses the compact union syntax.

reveal.text: def parse(value: str | bytes) -> str: ... uses the compact union syntax.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ | syntax is a type expression here; it should not be confused with the unrelated set/dict union operator used on runtime values.

reveal.text: The | syntax is a type expression here; it should not be confused with the unrelated set/dict union operator used on runtime values.

source_refs.title: What's new in Python 3.10 — union types

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ 3.10 officially supports grouping multiple context managers across lines inside parentheses after with.

reveal.text: Python 3.10 officially supports grouping multiple context managers across lines inside parentheses after with.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ (open(src) as inp, open(dst, 'w') as out): ... keeps a long multi-resource with statement readable.

reveal.text: with (open(src) as inp, open(dst, 'w') as out): ... keeps a long multi-resource with statement readable.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ context managers are still entered left-to-right and exited in reverse order.

reveal.text: All context managers are still entered left-to-right and exited in reverse order.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ 3.10 added strict= to zip(); when true, a length mismatch raises ValueError instead of silently truncating.

reveal.text: Python 3.10 added strict= to zip(); when true, a length mismatch raises ValueError instead of silently truncating.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________(zip(ids, scores, strict=True)) is a practical data-integrity pattern when each id must have exactly one score.

reveal.text: dict(zip(ids, scores, strict=True)) is a practical data-integrity pattern when each id must have exactly one score.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________=True detects mismatched lengths during iteration, because zip itself remains lazy.

reveal.text: strict=True detects mismatched lengths during iteration, because zip itself remains lazy.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ 3.10 added built-in aiter() and anext() helpers for working directly with asynchronous iterators.

reveal.text: Python 3.10 added built-in aiter() and anext() helpers for working directly with asynchronous iterators.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ = aiter(source); item = await anext(iterator) mirrors iter()/next() for async iteration.

reveal.text: iterator = aiter(source); item = await anext(iterator) mirrors iter()/next() for async iteration.
